grammar.title: Type 2 Conditionals — Si + Imperfect Subjunctive + Conditional
grammar.content:
Type 2 conditionals express hypothetical or unlikely situations in the present or future — the realm of dreams, advice, and counterfactual statements. The structure is strict:

Structure: Si + [imperfect subjunctive], [conditional]
Or reversed: [conditional] si + [imperfect subjunctive]

⚠️ CRITICAL ERROR TO AVOID: Never put the conditional after 'si'. 'Si tendría dinero' is grammatically incorrect. The correct form is 'Si tuviera dinero'.

Uses:
- Imagining unreal present situations: Si fuera rico, viajaría por el mundo
- Giving advice: Si yo fuera tú, no aceptaría ese trabajo
- Describing unlikely future events: Si ganáramos la lotería, compraríamos una casa

Imperfect subjunctive (-ra form) in the 'si' clause:
- yo: -ra
- tú: -ras
- él/ella/usted: -ra
- nosotros: -ramos
- vosotros: -rais
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -ran

Conditional in the result clause:
- yo: -ría
- tú: -rías
- él/ella/usted: -ría
- nosotros: -ríamos
- vosotros: -ríais
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -rían

rows: Si yo tuviera / tuviese más tiempo…
Si yo fuera tú, estudiaría más
Viajaría por Europa si tuviera dinero

examples: Si tuviera más dinero, compraría una casa en la playa. (If I had more money, I would buy a house on the beach.)
Si yo fuera tú, aceptaría esa oferta de trabajo. (If I were you, I would accept that job offer.)
Viajaríamos por Sudamérica si no tuviéramos que trabajar. (We would travel through South America if we didn't have to work.)
Si hablara español, podría conseguir un mejor empleo. (If I spoke Spanish, I could get a better job.)
¿Te gustaría ir a Japón si tuvieras la oportunidad? (Would you like to go to Japan if you had the chance?)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian Type 2 conditionals use a very similar structure: 'Dacă aș avea mai mult timp, aș călători prin Europa' — 'Dacă' = 'si', 'aș avea' = imperfect subjunctive equivalent, 'aș călători' = conditional. The mental mapping is nearly identical! Also note the same prohibition: never use the conditional directly after 'dacă' for unreal conditions.

pronunciation.title: Stress in Type 2 Conditionals
pronunciation.content:
Imperfect subjunctive forms are stressed on the ending:
- tuviera (too-BYE-ra) — stress on 'ie'
- hablara (ah-BLA-ra) — stress on 'ra'
- fuera (fweh-RAH) — stress on 'ra'

Conditional forms are also stressed on the ending:
- viajaría (bee-ah-REE-ah) — stress on 'rí'
- compraría (kom-prah-REE-ah) — stress on 'rí'
- aceptaría (ah-sep-TA-ree-ah) — stress on 'rí'

The accent marks on the -ía endings are always present in the conditional.

Critical: Spanish 'viajaría' is pronounced 'bee-ah-REE-ah' (5 syllables), NOT 'vee-ah-REE-ah' as English speakers might assume. The 'i' and 'a' in -ría are two separate syllables.
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian stress patterns are similar — most verb endings carry the stress. The Spanish conditional -ría is phonetically distinct from Romanian 'aș' + infinitive, which is two words.

exercises.question: Which sentence correctly uses Type 2 conditional structure?
exercises.explanation: Hypothetical 'if' clauses in the present require the imperfect subjunctive after 'si': 'Si tuviera dinero, viajaría.' Never use the conditional after 'si'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Si yo ____ (ser) tú, aceptaría esa oferta.' (If I were you, I would accept that offer.)
exercises.explanation: 'Fuera' — imperfect subjunctive of ser for yo/él/ella/usted. 'Si yo fuera tú' = If I were you.

exercises.question: What tense is used in the 'si' clause of a Type 2 conditional?
exercises.explanation: The 'si' clause always uses the imperfect subjunctive in Type 2 conditionals: Si tuviera..., Si pudiera..., Si hablara...

exercises.question: Complete: 'Viajaríamos por Sudamérica si ____ (tener) que trabajar.' (We would travel through South America if we didn't have to work.)
exercises.explanation: 'No tuviéramos' — imperfect subjunctive of tener for nosotros. Reversed order (no comma needed): 'Viajaríamos... si tuviéramos...'

exercises.question: Complete: 'Si ____ (you) hablara español, podría conseguir un mejor empleo.' (If you spoke Spanish, I could get a better job.)
exercises.explanation: 'Si tú hablara español' — imperfect subjunctive of hablar for tú: 'hablaras'. But the exercise asks for the pronoun. 'Si tú hablaras español, podría conseguir un mejor empleo.'

exercises.question: Complete the conditional tense conjugation for the verb GUSTAR:
exercises.explanation: Gustar uses conditional endings on the full infinitive: me gustaría, te gustaría, le gustaría, nos gustaría, os gustaría, les gustaría.
